summary.one_liner: Diagrams is a Python library for drawing cloud and system architecture diagrams as code, rendered through Graphviz.
summary.what_it_does: The library lets you describe architecture diagrams in Python code instead of using a design tool, which is useful for prototyping new system designs or documenting existing ones. It provides node sets for major cloud providers including AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, Alibaba Cloud and Oracle Cloud, plus on-premises nodes, SaaS services and programming frameworks and languages. Diagrams are rendered with Graphviz. Because the diagram is code, changes can be tracked in version control. The README states it does not control real cloud resources or generate CloudFormation or Terraform code. An online playground is also described for trying it in the browser.
use_cases: prototype a cloud architecture before building it
document an existing system architecture as a diagram
generate architecture diagrams from Python scripts
track architecture diagram changes in version control
visualize Kubernetes or cloud infrastructure layouts
how_to_run: Install Graphviz (for macOS: brew install graphviz)
Try the online playground at diagrams.mingrammer.com/playground without installing
notable: Diagrams are written as Python code, so they can be versioned and diffed
Node sets for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, Alibaba Cloud, Oracle Cloud and more
Online playground runs the package in the browser via Pyodide with PNG/SVG/JPEG export
Has a Go counterpart, go-diagrams, mentioned in the README
caveats: Requires a separate Graphviz installation for rendering
Does not manage real cloud resources or generate CloudFormation or Terraform code
